name: High-heat welding kit
description: An arc welder packed with a folded fireproof blanket that holds heat around the joint, so hardened and tempered steel can be welded without cracking.
notes: A blue welder case 300 by 220 by 220 mm with a dial, sockets and carry handle, standing on a folded flame-resistant blanket 500 by 360 mm, with the cable coiled beside it and the electrode holder and earth clamp in front. The box counts the air around the welder on the wider blanket and the handle. cloth-turnout stands in for the blanket. welding is a new quality name; 2 marks it above a plain welder because the kit is for tempered steel. It needs electric power, which has no content field yet.

name: Wire drawing machine
description: A bench machine that pulls steel rod through a block of narrowing dies onto a cranked drum, thinning it into wire.
notes: A steel base 500 by 240 mm with a die block of six tapering holes at one end and a capstan drum 160 mm across with a top crank at the other, a length of wire running between them. wire_drawing is the name batch 063 gave a hand drawplate at 1, and this machine draws more and finer wire, so 2. It works where it stands, so it carries the quality as a workstation, not a hand tool.

name: Wooden float
description: A long pine board with a grip nailed on top, for spreading and smoothing wet concrete or mortar. Swung edge-on, it makes a clumsy club.
notes: A board 610 by 120 by 22 mm with a round oak grip on two blocks, 92 mm tall overall. Box volume x1.99 is the air under the grip. planing 1 is the hand end of the planing scale, which takes in smoothing wood and wet finishes. It is made by the player, never found, so it has no spawn tiers.

name: Giant pipe wrench
description: A pipe wrench as long as a man's leg, with a red iron handle and toothed jaws that open wide enough for water mains. Far too heavy to carry around for long.
notes: Lies flat: a red I-beam handle 1.2 m overall, a cast frame with a knurled adjusting nut, a toothed heel jaw and a hook jaw on a shank across the frame, opening 120 mm. The box counts the jaw opening and the shank standing out across the frame. wrenching 3 because it turns pipe and fittings no hand wrench can, though it is too large for nuts and bolts. A melee use as a heavy club has no content field here.

name: Large adjustable wrench
description: A long adjustable spanner whose jaws open past two inches, with enough leverage for wheel nuts and stuck bolts.
notes: Shares a local adjustable-spanner builder with the small wrench: a tapered handle with a hang hole, a round head, two jaws and a knurled worm, 460 mm long. The jaw opening and the head's width over the handle leave air in the box. wrenching 2 marks an adjustable or large wrench; quick wheel change folds into wrenching.

name: Small adjustable wrench
description: A palm-sized adjustable spanner for small nuts and bolts in tight spaces.
notes: The large wrench's builder at 150 mm. wrenching 1 marks a small wrench; fine bolt-turning folds into it.

name: Craft knife
description: A slim pen-shaped handle holding a tiny pointed blade, made for precise cuts in paper, cloth and thin plastic. It cuts deep but barely reaches.
notes: A ribbed 9 mm handle, a tapered collet and an angled pointed blade, 100 mm long; the blade is drawn 2 mm thick because 2 mm is the finest grain. cutting 2 marks a precision blade; fine and cloth cutting fold into it. butchering is held at 1, the low end, because the blade is too short to joint a carcass.

name: Fidget spinner
description: A three-lobed plastic toy that spins on a bearing between finger and thumb. It does nothing useful, which used to be the point.
notes: Lies flat: a blue three-lobed body about 95 mm across with a centre bearing under black caps and a steel weight ring in each lobe. A morale use has no content field yet.
